html:
The first empire to cover most of the Indian subcontinent. It was founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 322 BCE, ruled from Pataliputra in Magadha, and lasted until 185 BCE.

Chandragupta, helped by the Brahmin advisor Chanakya, overthrew the Nanda kings of Magadha. He then moved into the northwest, which Alexander had just left in disorder. Around 305 BCE he fought and then made a treaty with Alexander's general Seleucus, gaining Afghanistan and Baluchistan in return for 500 war elephants. The Greek envoy Megasthenes lived at his court and wrote a description of India that survives in pieces.

The three great emperors:

  • Chandragupta (about 322 to 297 BCE) built the empire. Jain tradition says he gave up the throne and died as a monk.
  • Bindusara (about 297 to 273 BCE) pushed it south into the Deccan.
  • Ashoka (about 268 to 232 BCE) conquered Kalinga in the bloody Kalinga War, then turned to Buddhism and a policy of moral rule. His edicts, carved on rocks and pillars across the empire, are the empire's own voice and the oldest readable writing in India.

The empire had a large army and bureaucracy, a royal road from Bengal to the northwest (an ancestor of the Grand Trunk Road), and strong patronage of Buddhism and Jainism. The Great Stupa at Sanchi was begun in Ashoka's time.

After Ashoka it shrank quickly. In 185 BCE the general Pushyamitra Shunga killed the last emperor during a parade and founded the Shunga dynasty. Greek kings from Bactria soon moved into the northwest.
sum: The first empire to cover most of the Indian subcontinent. It was founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 322 BCE, ruled from Pataliputra in Magadha, and lasted until 185 BCE.
